title: PE and PPE families
dek: GC-rich, repeat-rich, secretion-associated gene families that wreck alignments and carry antigenic variation. Mask them for phylogeny; do not pretend they are junk.
story: PE and PPE proteins are named for N-terminal Pro-Glu and Pro-Pro-Glu motifs. They occupy a startling fraction of the Mtb coding genome. Subfamilies (PE_PGRS, PPE-MPTR) are GC-rich and full of repeats — exactly the sequence that short-read mappers duplicate, drop, or misalign.

Several PE/PPE proteins are ESX substrates (ESX-1, ESX-5 especially). They contribute to cell-wall remodelling, macrophage signalling, and antigenic variation. That is biology. It is also why a 20-SNP “cluster” that lives entirely inside PE_PGRS genes is usually a mapping artefact.

gDST catalogues mostly ignore PE/PPE for resistance grading. Phylogeny pipelines mask them. Immunology papers live in them. A lab that uses one BAM for all three tasks without saying so will lie at least once.
deep: Mask lists (e.g. the van Embden / Comas / extra PE-PPE beds) should be versioned in the methods. Changing the mask changes SNP distance.
Long reads recover some PE_PGRS structure that Illumina cannot. Do not over-interpret structural variants in these genes from 150-bp PE data.
ESX-5 is associated with PPE secretion and is essential in Mtb; ESX-1 is associated with ESAT-6/CFP-10 and virulence. Family membership is not a DST result.
Do not bulk-copy Mycobrowser PE_PGRS annotations into a clinical report. Name the mask, name the catalogue, stop.

example.title: A cluster that vanished on mask
example.setup: Three isolates, 8–11 SNPs pairwise unmasked. After PE/PPE mask, 0–1 SNPs. No shared rare DR mutations.

steps.title: Inspect where the SNPs sat
steps.body: If they pile in PE_PGRS with low mapping quality, they were never phylogeny.

steps.title: Report the masked distance
steps.body: These are the same strain by the programme SOP, plus mapping noise.

steps.title: Do not invent a super-spreader from unmasked SNPs
steps.body: Epidemiology follows the masked core, not the repeat dust.

example.takeaway: PE/PPE SNPs are guilty until the BAM says otherwise.

check.prompt: Why do MTBC transmission pipelines commonly mask PE/PPE genes?
choices: Because GC-rich repeats generate false SNPs that inflate distances
Because WHO catalogues grade them as high-confidence BDQ-R
Because they are absent from H37Rv
check.answer: Because GC-rich repeats generate false SNPs that inflate distances
check.why: Mapping artefact, not a moral judgement on the genes’ biology.

whyWrong.Because they encode rpoB: rpoB is not a PE gene.
